profiles.summary: No opcode result on any Ethereum build reached on 2026-11-27 differs from the specification. New this cycle: erigon's main branch (3.9.0-dev) adds handler shortcuts for DIV by a power of two, EXP and MULMOD with a cached reciprocal on top of an untagged uint256 commit, all on FullMath.mulDiv's path; they were transcribed and match on 2,190,028 vectors. sentio-super-node moved to v2.596.0 and runs the 200,127 vectors without a mismatch.

deltas.delta: erigon main (db/version/app.go: 3.9.0-dev) pins github.com/holiman/uint256 v1.3.3-0.20261109190209-808a9d02b85f, a master commit of 2026-11-09 that no earlier cycle read. erigon v3.8.2 pins 087f4b32f234 (read in cycle 24), geth v1.17.10 and master pin v1.3.2, and uint256 master is still de2a038 (F-163). Against v1.3.2, 808a9d02 adds umod with rem5by4, rem4by3 and rem3by2 to div.go and rewrites Div, Mod, SDiv and SMod in uint256.go; its div.go differs from de2a038 in 81 lines and its uint256.go in 94. mod.go (Reciprocal, reduce4) is byte equal in v1.3.2, 808a9d02 and de2a038. No erigon release carries 808a9d02: tags v3.8.3, v3.9.0 and v3.9.0-rc.1 and branch release/3.9 return 404.

erigon main's execution/vm/instructions.go changes handlers that the PoolManager's math runs. opDiv (lines 78-103) returns x >> n when the divisor is 2^n (log2Exact), which is every DIV at FullMath.sol:62, :67 and :73. opExp (lines 142-216) adds a base 2^256 - 1 case, an odd-base case for exponents of 2^64 or more that replaces the squarings above bit 62 by a binomial series (expOdd), and a uint64 loop for small products. opMulmod (lines 374-388) keeps the last modulus of 2^192 or more and its reciprocal in the CallContext and reduces through MulModWithReciprocal, which is the modulus not(0) at FullMath.sol:24. opCallDataLoad (lines 503-523) and the PUSH handlers (lines 1692-1733) take new fast paths. The cache fields are set in one statement and keyed by the full modulus (interpreter.go lines 105-108). None of this is in v3.8.2.

mainnet.rpc.sentio.xyz now answers sentio-super-node/v2.596.0-2c2c6b02304be9f31cbf86c5f01a99f86f25dc0d go1.26.3 (cycle 33: v2.595.0-35a27224). Its execution errors use the go-ethereum core/vm strings ('invalid opcode: INVALID', 'out of gas'), as geth and erigon do and reth does not. Its namespace errors are gRPC code 5 ('method ... not found'), and its eth_getProof puts accountProof after storageHash, an order neither geth's nor erigon's response uses. Sentio's SDK names the service an 'rpc-node/super-node proxy'.

profiles.summary: erigon main adds two caches to each call frame: the last two SLOAD results, valid while a state read stamp is unchanged, and a SELFBALANCE memo. The SELFBALANCE memo is already in v3.8.2 and does not reach any value the PoolManager computes. The SLOAD cache sits on every re-read of pool state after a hook call, and the definition of the stamp it trusts was not found.

deltas.delta: erigon main keeps a per-frame cache of the last two SLOAD results (frameSlots, interpreter.go lines 124-171; opSload, instructions.go lines 859-880). A hit needs the stack word to match and IntraBlockState.ReadStamp() to equal the stamp taken after the cached read. The cache is reset when a context returns to the pool (interpreter.go lines 251-253) and switched on per frame when ReadStamp reports it usable (line 577); a test says a serial state reports it usable and read tracing switches it off (execution/state/read_stamp_test.go). The ReadStamp function itself is not in execution/state/intra_block_state.go, journal.go, versionmap.go, versionedio.go or access_list.go at main.

erigon v3.8.2 and main memoize SELFBALANCE per frame (contract.go selfBalance, eips.go opSelfBalance) and clear the memo in CREATE, CALL, CALLCODE and DELEGATECALL; main also clears it in STATICCALL inside frame transactions, where APPROVE can debit the payer. A frame's own balance changes only through those opcodes, so the memo returns the current balance.

findings.title: Erigon's main branch rewrites DIV, EXP and MULMOD handlers on FullMath's path and caches storage reads per frame, and no release carries either yet
findings.difference: erigon main, the code its next release (3.9.0) will be cut from, computes DIV by a power of two as a right shift, EXP with an odd base and a large exponent by a binomial series, and MULMOD with a modulus of 2^192 or more through a reciprocal cached in the call frame, on uint256 commit 808a9d02 that no client release pins. It also returns SLOAD results from a two-entry per-frame cache while a state read stamp is unchanged. Geth, reth and Nethermind run none of this.
findings.mechanism: FullMath.mulDiv computes mulmod(a, b, not(0)) at FullMath.sol:24, then on the 512 bit path mulmod(a, b, denominator) at :48 and three divisions by twos, a power of two, at :62, :67 and :73. On erigon main the first two go through the cached reciprocal whenever the modulus is 2^192 or more, and the three divisions go through log2Exact and Rsh. SqrtPriceMath and SwapMath call mulDiv on every swap step, so a wrong shortcut would change prices and amounts in blocks an erigon validator builds or checks, and that validator would part from the other clients. This cycle copied the four handlers verbatim into a harness linked with uint256 808a9d02 and ran 1,845,864 vectors of cycle 29 (every opcode the PoolManager uses), 224,164 vectors aimed at the shortcuts (DIV by 2^n and its neighbours for all n, EXP with base 2^256 - 1, odd bases with exponents from 2^64 to 2^256 - 1 and the small loop, MULMOD runs that reuse one modulus with zero operands on a cache hit) and 120,000 FullMath division triples: no mismatch. Two planted changes were caught (20,747 and 262 mismatches) and a third, a stale reciprocal, made the harness stop answering. CALLDATALOAD and PUSH fast paths gave the v3.8.2 and specified result on 4,000,000 random cases. The SLOAD cache meets PoolManager.swap, which reads slot0 at PoolManager.sol:196, calls the hook at :202 (the hook may reenter and change the pool) and reads the pool again in _swap at :206; it is right only if every storage write and every revert changes the stamp, and the stamp's definition was not found.
findings.impact: None for funds today. A fault in these paths on an erigon validator would give that node a different state root, which the other clients reject; it is a consensus split for the operator, not a transfer of pool funds by an ordinary account. Simulated calls on an erigon RPC node would quote other amounts.
findings.preconditions: An erigon release cut from main, and a fault in one of the rewritten paths. The arithmetic paths tested clean; the SLOAD cache is unverified.
findings.mitigations: Run the vector sets and the reentrant hook scenarios on the first erigon 3.9 release before relying on erigon nodes for quotes. Validators can keep the client mix.

cleared.check: erigon main's DIV, EXP and MULMOD handlers on uint256 808a9d02, with the PoolManager's operand shapes (FullMath.sol:24, :48, :62, :67, :73).
cleared.result: 2,190,028 vectors through the verbatim handlers give the Python result: 1,845,864 of cycle 29, 224,164 aimed at the shortcuts and 120,000 FullMath division triples. MULMOD with a modulus below 2^192 still goes through MulMod; at or above it, the cached reciprocal is always the one Reciprocal returns for an equal modulus, and reduce4 is byte equal to v1.3.2's. expOdd is right as read: for an odd base b, b^(2^62) = 1 + u with u divisible by 2^64, so u^4 vanishes mod 2^256 and C(h,3) is needed only mod 2^64, which the product shifted by one and multiplied by the inverse of 3 gives.

cleared.check: erigon main's CALLDATALOAD fast path and the masked PUSH load, against v3.8.2's getData path and the specified zero padding.
cleared.result: 4,000,000 random cases (offsets inside, at and past the end of calldata, near 2^64 and above it; PUSH1 to PUSH32 at every position of short code) give the same word. The PoolManager's 44 CALLDATALOAD sites and every push therefore read the same values.

cleared.check: Can the SELFBALANCE memo of erigon v3.8.2 and main change a value the PoolManager computes?
cleared.result: No. The bytecode built from this checkout has one SELFBALANCE, from the native arm of Currency.balanceOfSelf (src/types/Currency.sol:90-95). Its only callers, sync and _settle, call it in their ERC-20 arms (src/PoolManager.sol:285 and :359), after isAddressZero has sent native currency elsewhere (:281-283 and :352-354). The memo is also cleared by every opcode that can move the frame's balance.

cleared.check: Upcoming forks within six months, assumed shipped: Glamsterdam with the 20 EIPs that EIP-7773 schedules, and Hegota with FOCIL and frame transactions (EIP-8081), against what cycles 21, 29, 31 and 33 cleared.
cleared.result: EIP-7773 and EIP-8081 are byte equal to the earlier copies, as are EIP-7778, 8024, 8037, 8038 and 8141, eth_config on reth v2.11.0 equals cycle 33's object (fork id 0x07c9462e, no next fork), and ethereum.org shows 'Mainnet date not yet set'. The earlier clearances stand. erigon main already carries Amsterdam code paths (EIP-8246 SELFDESTRUCT without burn, APPROVE inside STATICCALL for frame transactions) next to the rewritten handlers, so the client mix on the day after Glamsterdam may include the new erigon handlers.

leads.question: When erigon 3.9.0 is tagged, which uint256 commit does it pin, and are opDiv, opExp, opMulmod, opCallDataLoad, the PUSH handlers and frameSlots still those of main on 2026-11-27? Rerun build/herigon and scripts/erigon_fastpaths.py on the tagged code.
leads.why: The tests of this cycle cover the main branch only; a release may pin de2a038 or later, whose div.go differs from 808a9d02 in 81 lines.

leadResults.answer: sentio-super-node is Sentio's own service; Sentio's SDK calls it an 'rpc-node/super-node proxy'. Its execution errors are the go-ethereum core/vm strings, so it embeds a go-ethereum lineage EVM, but its response layer is its own (gRPC code 5 for unknown methods, a field order in eth_getProof that neither geth nor erigon uses), and no source or EVM version is published. It moved to v2.596.0-2c2c6b02 on 2026-11-27 and ran all 200,127 vectors with no mismatch. The two script sets did not complete through its rate limit this cycle either, so the whole PoolManager bytecode has still not run there.

76 known Ethereum endpoints were asked for web3_clientVersion on 2026-11-27 and chainlist.org lists no endpoint outside that set. None names Nethermind or Besu. The answering builds are reth v2.2.0 to v2.11.0, Geth v1.16.7 to v1.17.10, erigon 3.6.0 to 3.8.2 and sentio-super-node v2.596.0.
